## Summary

**Root cause** — In `source/src/atomate2/common/schemas/elastic.py`, `_expand_deformations` used `Deformation.is_independent()` to validate symmetry-rotated deformations. That method counts perturbed entries of the **deformation gradient**, but shear strains produce Cholesky gradients that perturb *two* entries (an off-diagonal plus a compensating diagonal). So every symmetry-rotated shear equivalent was discarded. The fit ended up with 14 deformations (only `yz`-shear survived; `xz`/`xy` and the `+m` shears were lost), driving raw `C55=C66=0`. `convert_to_ieee` → `fit_to_structure` then averaged the surviving `C44≈94.7` with the two zeros, yielding IEEE `C44=C55=C66≈31.5` — unreconcilable with the stress-strain ratio of ~94.7.

**The fix** (`_expand_deformations`):
- Replaced the deformation-gradient `is_independent()` check with a **strain-based** independence check: a rotated deformation is kept only if its Green-Lagrange strain has exactly one nonzero Voigt component (`_is_independent_strain`). This correctly recognizes shears as independent.
- Changed deduplication to key on the **Green-Lagrange strain** rather than the deformation gradient. Multiple rotated shear deformations can realize the same strain (Cholesky is not unique under rotation); keeping more than one would duplicate strain magnitudes and make the finite-difference Vandermonde system singular.

The change is general — it operates on strain Voigt components and symmetry, with no structure, numeric, ID, or path hard-coding. It degrades gracefully to the original behavior for normal strains and for lower-symmetry crystals whose point-group ops don't map pure strains to pure strains.
